---
title: "Foreign-Connected PAC Contributions"
format: html
embed-resources: true
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
```

## a. Load all data

Read all 13 CSVs in a single `read_csv()` call, using the file name to derive the election cycle `year` (the second year in each file's cycle label, e.g. 1999-2000 → 2000).

```{r}
pac_raw <- read_csv(
  list.files("data", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE),
  id = "source"
) |>
  mutate(
    year = parse_number(str_extract(source, "\\d{4}(?=\\.csv$)")),
    .keep = "unused"
  )

pac_raw
```

## b. Clean names and transform

Clean variable names with `janitor::clean_names()`, split `country_of_origin_parent_company` into separate `country_of_origin` and `parent_company` columns, and convert the dollar-string amount columns to numeric.

```{r}
pac <- pac_raw |>
  clean_names() |>
  separate(
    country_of_origin_parent_company,
    into = c("country_of_origin", "parent_company"),
    sep = "/",
    extra = "merge"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    across(c(total, dems, repubs), ~ parse_number(.x))
  ) |>
  select(year, everything())

pac |> slice_head(n = 10)
```

## c. Pivot longer

Pivot so `dems`/`repubs` become a `party` column (`Democrat`/`Republican`) and an `amount` column.

```{r}
pac_long <- pac |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(dems, repubs),
    names_to = "party",
    values_to = "amount"
  ) |>
  mutate(party = recode(party, dems = "Democrat", repubs = "Republican")) |>
  select(-total)

pac_long |> slice_head(n = 10)
```

## d. UK-connected PAC totals by year and party

```{r}
uk_contributions <- pac_long |>
  filter(country_of_origin == "UK") |>
  summarise(total_amount = sum(amount, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(year, party)) |>
  arrange(year, party)

uk_contributions |> slice_head(n = 10)
```

## e. Visualization

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
ggplot(uk_contributions, aes(x = year, y = total_amount, color = party)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Democrat = "#2E74B5", Republican = "#C0504D")) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_dollar(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Election cycle",
    y = "Total contributions",
    color = "Party",
    title = "Contributions to US parties from UK-connected PACs, 2000–2024"
  )
```

**Design choices:** A line plot is appropriate here because contributions are tracked over time — lines emphasize trends and changes across election cycles better than bars would for a continuous total. Points mark the actual cycle observations. Party is mapped to color using conventional blue/red associations, with direct mapping through `color` rather than facets so the two parties can be compared on the same scale.

**What it reveals:** UK-connected PACs consistently gave more to Republicans than Democrats through about 2012, often by a wide margin (e.g. 2002–2006). Around 2014 the gap narrowed sharply, and from 2016 onward contributions to the two parties were roughly comparable, with Democrats even edging ahead in some recent cycles. Total giving rose substantially over the period — from under $2M per cycle per party in the early 2000s to peaks around $4–6M — with a noticeable dip for Republicans in 2020 before rebounding in 2024.
